blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Prove by mathematical induction that for all positive integral values of \(n\): \(n^2 + n\) is divisible by 2
blocks.explanation:
Yeh divisibility (taqseem) ka sawal hai. "Divisible by 2" ka matlab hai: expression \(= 2 \times\) (koi integer). Is shakal mein likhne se algebra ke zariye saboot dena aasaan ho jata hai.
Isay har positive integer \(n\) ke liye induction se saabit karna hai.
Plan: \((k + 1)^2 + (k + 1)\) ko expand karna, us ke andar purana expression \(k^2 + k\) dhoondna, us ki jagah \(2m\) rakhna, aur 2 common nikalna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(S(n): n^2 + n\) 2 se divisible hai.
Saabit karna hai: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sahi hai.
Tareeqa: Mathematical induction. "2 se divisible" ko equation bana lein: \(n^2 + n = 2m\), jahan \(m\) koi integer hai.

Base case: \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[1^2 + 1 = 2 = 2 \times 1\]
Is liye \(S(1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: 2 khud 2 ka multiple hai (\(2 \times 1\)).

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein
\[k^2 + k = 2m,\ m \in \mathbb{Z} \quad (A)\]
Kyun: \(S(k)\) kehta hai ke \(k^2 + k\) 2 se divisible hai, yani yeh 2 aur kisi integer \(m\) ka product hai. \(\mathbb{Z}\) ka matlab integers ka set hai.

Target \(S(k + 1)\)
\[(k + 1)^2 + (k + 1)\ \text{is divisible by 2}\]
Kyun: \(n = k + 1\) rakha.

Inductive step: expand kar ke (A) lagayein
\[(k + 1)^2 + (k + 1)\]
\[= k^2 + 2k + 1 + k + 1\]
\[= (k^2 + k) + 2k + 2\]
\[= 2m + 2(k + 1)\]
\[= 2(m + k + 1)\]
Kyun: Expand karne ke baad terms ko is tarah tarteeb di ke purana tukra \(k^2 + k\) alag nazar aaye; (A) se us ki jagah \(2m\) rakha. Baaqi \(2k + 2 = 2(k + 1)\) bhi 2 ka multiple hai. Ab dono hisson mein 2 common hai.
Dhyan dein: Induction ka asal hunar yahi hai: naye expression mein purane expression ko "dhoond kar" bahar nikalna.

Nateeja parhein
\(m + k + 1\) integer hai, is liye \((k + 1)^2 + (k + 1)\) 2 se divisible hai. Yani \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: Integers ka jama hamesha integer hota hai, is liye bracket wala number poora number hai.

Conclusion
\(S(1)\) sahi hai aur \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of mathematical induction se \(n^2 + n\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 2 se divisible hai.
Kyun: Induction ki dono sharten poori ho gayin.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 5\)
\[5^2 + 5 = 30 = 2 \times 15 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Ek aur nazar se: \(n^2 + n = n(n + 1)\) do lagatar numbers ka product hai, aur do lagatar numbers mein se ek hamesha even hota hai. Is liye jawab hamesha even aata hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(n^2 + n\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 2 se divisible hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Prove by mathematical induction that for all positive integral values of \(n\): \(5^n - 2^n\) is divisible by 3
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi divisibility ka sawal hai, lekin powers ke saath: dikhana hai ke \(5^n - 2^n = 3 \times\) (koi integer).
Isay har positive integer \(n\) ke liye induction se saabit karna hai.
Plan: hypothesis se \(5^k = 2^k + 3m\) likhna; phir \(5^{k+1}\) ko \(5 \cdot 5^k\) mein torna, \(5^k\) ki jagah value rakhna, aur 3 common nikalna. Powers wale divisibility sawalon ka yahi standard tareeqa hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(S(n): 5^n - 2^n\) 3 se divisible hai.
Saabit karna hai: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sahi hai.
Tareeqa: Mathematical induction. "3 se divisible" ko \(5^n - 2^n = 3m\) likhenge, jahan \(m\) integer hai.

Base case: \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[5^1 - 2^1 = 3 = 3 \times 1\]
Is liye \(S(1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: 3 khud 3 ka multiple hai.

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein
\[5^k - 2^k = 3m,\ m \in \mathbb{Z}\]
\[5^k = 2^k + 3m \quad (A)\]
Kyun: Hum bari power \(5^k\) ko akela kar lete hain, taake inductive step mein us ki jagah seedha \(2^k + 3m\) rakh sakein. Yeh chhota sa qadam aage ka kaam bahut aasaan kar deta hai.

Target \(S(k + 1)\)
\[5^{k+1} - 2^{k+1}\ \text{is divisible by 3}\]
Kyun: \(n = k + 1\) rakha.

Inductive step: powers ko torein aur (A) lagayein
\[5^{k+1} - 2^{k+1} = 5 \cdot 5^k - 2 \cdot 2^k\]
\[= 5(2^k + 3m) - 2 \cdot 2^k\]
\[= 5 \cdot 2^k + 15m - 2 \cdot 2^k\]
\[= 3 \cdot 2^k + 15m\]
\[= 3(2^k + 5m)\]
Kyun: Law of indices se \(5^{k+1} = 5 \times 5^k\) aur \(2^{k+1} = 2 \times 2^k\). Is tarah \(5^k\) saamne aa gaya aur (A) se us ki jagah \(2^k + 3m\) rakha. Ab \(2^k\) ko ek cheez samjhein: paanch \(2^k\) mein se do \(2^k\) nikalein to teen \(2^k\) bachte hain. Aakhir mein \(3 \cdot 2^k\) aur \(15m\) dono mein 3 common hai.
Dhyan dein: \(5 \cdot 5^k\) ko \(25^k\) likhna ghalat hai; yeh \(5^{k+1}\) hai.

Nateeja parhein
\(2^k + 5m\) integer hai, is liye \(5^{k+1} - 2^{k+1}\) 3 se divisible hai. Yani \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: \(2^k\) bhi integer hai aur \(5m\) bhi, aur integers ka jama integer hota hai.

Conclusion
\(S(1)\) sahi hai aur \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of mathematical induction se \(5^n - 2^n\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 3 se divisible hai.
Kyun: Induction ki dono sharten poori ho gayin.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 3\)
\[125 - 8 = 117 = 3 \times 39 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: 117 ke digits ka jama \(1 + 1 + 7 = 9\) hai, jo 3 se divisible hai; is liye 117 bhi 3 se divisible hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(5^n - 2^n\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 3 se divisible hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Prove by mathematical induction that for all positive integral values of \(n\): \(8 \times 10^n - 2\) is divisible by 6
blocks.explanation:
Yeh divisibility ka sawal hai: dikhana hai ke \(8 \times 10^n - 2 = 6 \times\) (koi integer).
Isay har positive integer \(n\) ke liye induction se saabit karna hai.
Plan: hypothesis se \(8 \times 10^k = 6m + 2\) likhna; phir \(10^{k+1}\) ko \(10 \cdot 10^k\) mein torna, value rakhna, aur 6 common nikalna. Bilkul part (ii) wala tareeqa.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(S(n): 8 \times 10^n - 2\) 6 se divisible hai.
Saabit karna hai: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sahi hai.
Tareeqa: Mathematical induction. "6 se divisible" ko \(8 \times 10^n - 2 = 6m\) likhenge, \(m\) integer.

Base case: \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[8 \times 10 - 2 = 78 = 6 \times 13\]
Is liye \(S(1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: 78 ko 6 se taqseem karein to 13 aata hai, koi baqi nahi bachta.

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein
\[8 \times 10^k - 2 = 6m,\ m \in \mathbb{Z}\]
\[8 \times 10^k = 6m + 2 \quad (A)\]
Kyun: Poore group \(8 \times 10^k\) ko akela kiya, taake inductive step mein us ki jagah \(6m + 2\) rakh sakein.

Target \(S(k + 1)\)
\[8 \times 10^{k+1} - 2\ \text{is divisible by 6}\]
Kyun: \(n = k + 1\) rakha.

Inductive step: ek 10 alag karein aur (A) lagayein
\[8 \times 10^{k+1} - 2 = 10(8 \times 10^k) - 2\]
\[= 10(6m + 2) - 2\]
\[= 60m + 20 - 2\]
\[= 60m + 18\]
\[= 6(10m + 3)\]
Kyun: \(10^{k+1} = 10 \times 10^k\), is liye \(8 \times 10^{k+1} = 10 \times (8 \times 10^k)\); is tarah purana group saamne aa gaya aur (A) se us ki jagah \(6m + 2\) rakha. Phir \(60m = 6 \times 10m\) aur \(18 = 6 \times 3\), is liye 6 common nikal aaya.
Dhyan dein: \(-2\) ko bhool kar sirf \(10 \times 2 = 20\) likhna aam ghalti hai; \(20 - 2 = 18\) hi 6 se divisible banta hai.

Nateeja parhein
\(10m + 3\) integer hai, is liye \(8 \times 10^{k+1} - 2\) 6 se divisible hai. Yani \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: \(m\) integer hai, to \(10m + 3\) bhi integer hai.

Conclusion
\(S(1)\) sahi hai aur \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of mathematical induction se \(8 \times 10^n - 2\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 6 se divisible hai.
Kyun: Induction ki dono sharten poori ho gayin.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 2\)
\[800 - 2 = 798 = 6 \times 133 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: 798 even hai (2 se divisible) aur digits ka jama 24 hai (3 se divisible), is liye 6 se bhi divisible hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(8 \times 10^n - 2\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 6 se divisible hai.
